guidance.procedure: Read every operative definition as one logical chain. Test breadth first: technical-only coverage requires a closed protected class confined to technical subject matter; any alternative covering business, financial, commercial, customer, personnel, marketing, or other information opposes exclusivity. Test identification separately: every route into the protected class must depend on the discloser’s marking or designation; an alternative based on nature, context, reasonable expectation, or confidentiality regardless of labeling opposes universal express identification. Oral or visual coverage supports verbal inclusion even when subject to contemporaneous designation or later written confirmation. Cite every fragment supplying an alternative route or condition and independently operative repeated definitions; exclude headings, recitals, exclusions, and adjacent examples that do not establish scope.

Build three independent lifecycle checks. For return or destruction, identify the operative disposition command and its exact trigger: termination or expiration supports a termination-triggered duty, but a request, demand, completion event, or end of discussions alone does not. For post-agreement retention, inspect the command’s full object and every archival, backup, legal-compliance, dispute, professional-record, or inaccessible-copy exception. An express exception permitting retained material supports some retention; an unconditional no-copy or no-retention command supports the opposed boundary; silence after a request-only clause settles neither. For survival, require confidentiality or use obligations expressly continuing after termination. A continuing solicitation restriction, fixed agreement term, antecedent-breach rule, ownership clause, or return duty is not confidentiality survival. Cite the trigger, disposition scope, responsive exceptions, and continuation language without borrowing evidence among these tests.

Decide employee disclosure, outsider disclosure, and copying independently. Match the receiving actor, action, recipient class, quantifier, and every attached condition. Employee access may be permitted while consultants, advisers, contractors, agents, affiliates, or other outsiders remain prohibited; outsider permission does not automatically answer employee access. A direct prohibition covering the queried class supports the restrictive boundary, but mere absence of permission does not. Discretionary written consent alone is not standing permission. For copying, a necessity- or purpose-limited exception permits some copying, whereas an absolute or consent-only prohibition opposes it. Cite each independently operative disclosure or copying rule and fragments supplying need-to-know, authorization, confidentiality, or purpose conditions. Exclude recipient-liability, notice, safeguarding, use, and neighboring-class provisions that do not govern the queried action.

Start with the operative exclusion or permission lead-in, then follow only the responsive continuation. Independent development must concern development without using, referring to, relying on, or accessing protected information. Third-party acquisition requires an external source entitled to disclose and, when stated, free of a confidentiality duty; independent development, prior possession, public availability, employee access, and descriptive definition text are not substitutes. Treat compelled-disclosure authority and notice as separate propositions: verify legal compulsion, an actual notice duty or express excuse, protective-order opportunity, and any required-portion limit. A heading or compelled-disclosure permission alone does not establish notice. Cite the lead-in when it supplies scope and every continuation completing the responsive exception; exclude neighboring exceptions even when grammatically adjacent. If the matching exception is absent, do not infer its opposite.

Match the regulated actor, modality, direct conduct, protected object or people, duration, and exceptions. Reverse engineering requires express reverse-engineer, decompile, disassemble, decrypt, decipher, reconstruct, re-identify, or materially equivalent conduct directed at protected material or an embodying product; a heading alone is insufficient, and copying, confidentiality, ownership, return, signature, or severability text is not a substitute. Solicitation requires recruiting, soliciting, inducing departure, hiring, or comparable conduct directed at the specified representatives; a restriction concerning only customers or business opportunities does not establish it. Cite every fragment completing the actor and restriction. If the direct conduct is absent, use absence rather than inventing an opposing permission.

Test rights and agreement secrecy separately. No-license requires operative language that no license, right, title, interest, option, or other right is granted or implied; ownership, restricted use, access, or a disclaimer alone is insufficient. Agreement confidentiality requires protection of the agreement's existence or terms, or of the fact, status, or substance of negotiations or discussions; an entire-agreement clause or ordinary confidentiality of disclosed information is not responsive. Cite every fragment carrying the protected subject and prohibition, excluding headings, signatures, purpose clauses, and neighboring ownership or use text.

Locate every operative provision that regulates the receiving actor’s use of protected information or directly qualifies the limited right to use it. Match the actor, protected object, permitted purpose, prohibited other purposes, and any exception or separate clause that narrows that permission. A recital describing why information is disclosed, a disclosure authorization, confidentiality duty, copying rule, ownership statement, or no-license clause is not by itself a use restriction. Conversely, do not omit an independently operative qualification merely because the principal purpose-limitation clause is already sufficient. Cite the complete actor-action-object-purpose chain and responsive qualifications; exclude neighboring agreement-secrecy, recipient-class, and intellectual-property language that supplies no use condition.

Evaluate breadth, identification, and oral form independently. Reconstruct every operative route into the protected class, including split continuations and repeated definitions. Technical-only coverage requires a closed class confined to technical matter; business, financial, commercial, customer, personnel, marketing, or other coverage opposes exclusivity. Universal express identification requires every route to depend on marking or designation; nature, context, reasonable-expectation, or presumed-confidential routes oppose it. Oral material qualifies when spoken disclosure can enter the class, even subject to designation or later confirmation. Cite all fragments creating the responsive route or condition, including illustrative categories when they establish breadth, but exclude headings, exclusions, and unrelated neighboring routes.

complete_original_evidence_texts: 1. Confidential Information means:

(i) technologies in written or tangible form disclosed to COMPANY from time to time after the Effective Date of this Agreement by ROCHESTER and identified with particularity at time of disclosure and marked confidential; and

(ii) technologies communicated orally or visually to COMPANY by ROCHESTER, if it is reduced to writing or other tangible form by ROCHESTER on or before the date thirty days after the date of such communication, marked confidential, and promptly delivered to COMPANY.

Confidential information also includes any information of the owner and a third party with which the Owner deals, including, but not limited to: financial information, business records, plans, trade secrets, product ideas, technical data of any type, contracts, billing records, pricing structure, discounts, property, investments, strategic alliances, partnerships, customer or client lists.
The nature of the information and manner of the disclosure are such that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential.
